_comment: Milestone 5: Mayan ASJP core vocabulary (31 languages, LexStat cognates). Ages in years before AD 2000 (ASJP lists are mostly 20th century). STATUS: DRAFT, every calibration and prior below must be checked by George and the supervisor before any date is reported. Glottochronological dates (e.g. Kaufman's ~2200 BC for Proto-Mayan, his subgroup dates) are deliberately NOT used as calibrations, since they would make the analysis circular: the root age is what we test against them.

root_age._why: Broad: contains every published Proto-Mayan estimate (c. 6600 BC to c. 209 BC, i.e. 8600-2209 BP) with margin, so the root is estimated, not assumed.

yule_birth_rate._why: Estimated; vague prior centred near 1e-3 per year.

loss_rate._why: Basic-vocabulary replacement of roughly 10-30% per millennium (mean ~2e-4 per class per year); sdlog 1 spans about an order of magnitude either way. This prior carries absolute-time information alongside the calibrations; it is a modelling choice to review.

calibrations.name: Yucatecan
calibrations.source: Hofling (2018) places Proto-Yucatecan at about AD 950 (about 1050 BP); Hofling (2006) and Aissen, England and Zavala Maldonado (eds., 2017) give Mopan as the first split. Subgroup monophyly is uncontroversial.
calibrations.status: soft; check whether Hofling's date is independent of glottochronology

calibrations.name: Huastecan
calibrations.source: Kaufman (1980:101), Kaufman and Justeson (2008), and Robertson and Houston (2015:32) place the differentiation of Chicomuceltec from Huastec in the Postclassic (here AD 900-1521). Qualitative, not glottochronological.

sensitivity_calibrations.name: Cholan
sensitivity_calibrations.source: Houston, Robertson and Stuart (2000, Current Anthropology 41:321-356): the Classic inscriptions (from c. AD 250) record Classic Ch'olti'an, ancestral to Eastern Cholan, which implies the Eastern/Western Cholan split predates c. 1750 BP.
sensitivity_calibrations.status: CONTESTED: Mora-Marin argues the shared traits are retentions and that Cholan diversification is Postclassic. Use only as a sensitivity analysis.
